learning: Check whether the stall progress moves from 0.155 when base_speed changes. If it stays at 0.155, the cause is the sensor coverage edge, not speed. Also compare slalom steering oscillation with the 0.150 seen in iteration 1.
notes: Holds the Builder's iteration 2 geometry (row at plus or minus 0.02 m, y=0.04, 12 mm) so the race isolates the controller. Gains are lowered (kp 1.0), damping raised (kd 0.4), and speed lowered (base_speed 1.1), because the 0.155 progress stall on two tracks points to an early, speed-related failure. Based on iteration 1 race data.
rationale: Iteration 1 gave 57.11 against 51.09 for iteration 0, so the narrower row helped a little. Progress still stopped at 0.155 on the oval and s-bend, the same value on both tracks, and every run went off track at max error about 0.063. The slalom oscillation barely moved (0.150 against 0.153), so the row narrowing and the forward move from y=0.06 to y=0.04 did not fix the oscillation. Iteration 1 also changed the controller (kp 2.0 to 1.2, kd 0.2 to 0.3, base_speed 1.6 to 1.3), so the race does not separate the two causes. The identical stall progress across tracks suggests a fixed failure point early in the course rather than a shape-specific one. I keep the Builder's iteration 2 geometry unchanged, as the Builder intended, so this race judges the controller alone. For the controller, I lower kp to 1.0 to reduce the steering response to the slalom's sharp reversals, raise kd to 0.4 for damping, and lower base_speed to 1.1 to reduce drift when the robot enters a bend at speed. ki stays at 0 to avoid windup, and line_loss stays last_direction. Expected result: steering oscillation on the slalom below 0.15, and the first line loss later in progress than 0.155. I do not expect completion yet. The race should show whether the stall point moves with speed; if it does not, the cause is the sensor coverage edge, not the gains.
